title: A Summit for the Provision
premise: Rafael Ishikawa, a riverboat captain hiding from a past he helped bury, is hired by his old rival Sable Voss to run the Kestrel River upstream to the glacier source before calving season seals it — a route they once swore off after it cost them their crew and Rafael's memory of the night his brother drowned. As the crew battles rapids, sabotage, and Voss's hidden agenda to claim a legendary provision cache, Rafael's fragmented memories resurface and force him to choose between duty to his crew and the truth about who betrayed them. In the end, Rafael reaches the source, confronts Voss, and learns his brother's death was an accident Voss concealed out of guilt; he lets the cache flood into the calving glacier, choosing love for his first mate Isela over vengeance, and returns downstream changed, no longer invisible but finally free.
about_author: Emrys Montrose is the pen name of a former deckhand turned writer who spent six seasons piloting cargo runs on glacial-fed rivers before trading the wheelhouse for a desk. Their fiction blends hard-won river lore with quiet meditations on grief, debt, and the water that carries both.

chapters.title: The Mood of Sandbars
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. A slow morning on the Kestrel Delta introduces the riverboat Marrow and its small crew, including first mate Isela, whom Rafael quietly loves. He pays off another installment of a mysterious debt to a harbor clerk. Emotional beat: contentment built on avoidance.

chapters.title: A Name He Buried
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Sable Voss arrives at the dock after nine years, offering triple pay to run upstream to the glacier source — the route sworn off since the disaster. Rafael refuses; Isela, seeing the crew's empty purse, argues they can't afford pride. Emotional beat: old wounds reopened.

chapters.title: Terms in Salt Water
chapters.summary: Isela's POV. The crew votes to take the job over Rafael's objection. Isela negotiates terms with Voss and notices Voss flinch at mention of Rafael's brother Tomas. She begins keeping her own ledger of lies. Emotional beat: loyalty pulling against suspicion.

chapters.title: Loading the Marrow
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Preparations reveal odd cargo: surveying gear, sealed crates, and a permit stamped with a ministry seal that shouldn't exist. Rafael's compass needle trembles near the crates. Emotional beat: dread disguised as routine.

chapters.title: First Rapids
chapters.summary: Deckhand Juno's POV. The Marrow fights the Lower Stair rapids; Juno proves herself and earns Rafael's trust. Voss handles a rope like someone trained on this exact river years ago. Emotional beat: camaraderie forged under pressure.

chapters.title: The Village That Isn't on Charts
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. A supply stop at an uncharted fishing village where an elder recognizes Rafael and calls him by a name he doesn't remember using. Fragments of memory surface: a fire, shouting, cold water. Emotional beat: the past refusing to stay sunk.

chapters.title: What Isela Saw
chapters.summary: Isela's POV. Isela catches Voss burning documents at night and reads a scrap: coordinates matching the source, dated the year of the disaster. She says nothing to Rafael yet, protecting him and testing her own conscience. Emotional beat: love as complicity.

chapters.title: The Toll Bridge
chapters.summary: Juno's POV. A river toll gang demands passage fees the crew can't pay; Voss pays with one of the sealed crates' contents — ministry-grade blasting permits. Juno realizes the job may be illegal. Emotional beat: innocence cracking.

chapters.title: Memory Like Cold Water
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. A nightmare sequence interwoven with waking flashbacks: Tomas on the ice, a rope cut clean, Rafael's own hands bleeding. He wakes with Isela watching him and almost tells her everything. Emotional beat: grief surfacing as physical terror.

chapters.title: Sabotage at the Narrows
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Someone loosens the rudder pins overnight; the Marrow nearly founders in the Narrows. Voss suspects his own hired hands are working for a rival syndicate. First glimpse of Voss's guilt about Tomas. Emotional beat: paranoia tightening the screws.

chapters.title: Halfway House
chapters.summary: Isela's POV. At an abandoned waystation, Isela finds Tomas's old journal hidden in a wall — pages describing the cache and Voss's original plan from nine years ago. She must decide whether Rafael should read it before the source. Emotional beat: the weight of knowing.

chapters.title: The Debt Collector
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. A syndicate skiff overtakes them: Rafael's 'debt' was never money — it was silence about the disaster, purchased by Voss all along. The collector warns them to turn back or forfeit more than coin. Emotional beat: betrayal reframing his whole life.

chapters.title: Confrontation in the Fog
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Rafael and Voss fight on deck in river fog; Voss admits he hired the crew because only Rafael knows the safe channel through the calving fields. The fight ends unresolved when foghorns signal the syndicate following. Emotional beat: hatred entangled with need.

chapters.title: Running the Syndicate
chapters.summary: Juno's POV. A chase through braided channels; Juno's quick thinking and Rafael's sandbar knowledge shake the pursuers, but the Marrow takes hull damage and loses a third of their fuel. Emotional beat: triumph shadowed by dwindling odds.

chapters.title: Isela's Choice
chapters.summary: Isela's POV. With the ship limping, Isela gives Rafael Tomas's journal. Reading it, Rafael learns Voss cut the rope to save Tomas, not kill him — and that Rafael himself, concussed, gave the order that put Tomas on the ice. Emotional beat: devastating reversal.

chapters.title: The Silent Watch
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Rafael stops speaking to anyone, steering through the night while memories fully return. Isela sits with him without words. He decides not to turn back — not for Voss, but to see the place where his brother died. Emotional beat: numb resolve.

chapters.title: Icefield Approach
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. The calving season's first groans echo downriver; the window is closing early. Voss confesses the full truth to Rafael privately: the cache is real, and Voss wanted Rafael there to share the blame he's carried. Emotional beat: confession without absolution.

chapters.title: The Source
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. They reach the forbidden source: a turquoise lake beneath the glacier holding the provision cache — supplies, records, and proof of the syndicate's crimes. The syndicate skiff arrives behind them. Emotional beat: awe colliding with siege.

chapters.title: Calving
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs in short cuts. The glacier calves; the lake surges. In the chaos, Voss sacrifices himself to free the trapped Marrow, shoving the crew clear as ice takes the cache and the syndicate boat. Emotional beat: sacrifice answering nine years of debt.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Isela's POV. Downstream of the surge, the crew salvages what matters: each other, and Tomas's journal. Isela and Rafael finally speak plainly of love amid loss. Emotional beat: tenderness after catastrophe.

chapters.title: Settling Accounts
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Back at the delta, Rafael settles his 'debt' by delivering Voss's confession and the surviving journal page to a ministry investigator, ending the syndicate's hold. He keeps nothing but the compass. Emotional beat: justice chosen over revenge.

chapters.title: A Summit for the Provision
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV, coda. Months later, Rafael pilots the repaired Marrow on ordinary runs, Isela at his side, Juno apprenticed at the wheel. He visits the uncharted village and gives the elder Tomas's compass bearing so the name is remembered. Emotional beat: peace earned, memory carried forward.
